drugs.phenotype: Patients with the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype and cystic fibrosis may not respond when treated with cysteamine as compared to patients with the CTT/del or del/del genotypes. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence the efficacy of cysteamine.

Patients with the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR F508del variant) and cystic fibrosis have an unknown response to lumacaftor treatment, as response may depend on the presence of other CFTR variants. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to lumacaftor.

Patients with cystic fibrosis and the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype may not respond to treatment with cavosonstat. However, conflicting evidence has been reported. Other clinical and genetic factors may also affect response to cavosonstat.

Patients with the rs75527207 AA genotype (two copies of the CFTR G551D variant) and cystic fibrosis may respond to ivacaftor/tezacaftor treatment. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to ivacaftor/tezacaftor.

Patients with the rs77010898 AA genotype and cystic fibrosis may receive benefit when treated with ivacaftor and curcumin as compared to patients with the GG genotype. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence the efficacy of ivacaftor and curcumin.

Patients with the rs113993959 GG genotype and cystic fibrosis may not have improvement in chloride transport when treated with ataluren. Randomized clinical trials did not find improvement in chloride transport or improved pulmonary function after 2 rounds of 2 weeks of treatment. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence changes in chloride transport and improvement of pulmonary symptoms in patients with cystic fibrosis.

Patients with the rs121909019 GG genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR R1066C variant) and cystic fibrosis may have decreased clinical benefit when treated with elexacaftor / tezacaftor / ivacaftor as compared to patients with the GT or TT genotype. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence elexacaftor / tezacaftor / ivacaftor clinical benefit.

data.text: PMID 42367968: "CFTR function in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes." (bioRxiv, 2026). Abstract: CFTR function in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes.. RATIONALE: An estimated 25 million people worldwide have one deleterious variant in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator ( CFTR ) gene. Chronic respiratory disease symptoms are at an increased prevalence in cystic fibrosis (CF) heterozygotes. OBJECTIVES: Determine the level of CFTR function in CF heterozygotes compared to individuals without CF-causing variants. Establish whether CFTR function differs between asymptomatic and symptomatic CF heterozygotes. METHODS: Individuals without respiratory symptoms or CF family history were recruited as controls. Heterozygotes were recruited from families with a CF individual harboring null alleles or c.1521_1523del (F508del) in CFTR . CFTR function was measured by short circuit current in primary human nasal epithelial cells (HNEs) from participants. Cell composition was assessed by single cell RNA sequencing. data.text: PMID 41953138: "CFTR gene variant detection in moroccan individuals via nanopore long-read sequencing." (Front Genet, 2026). Abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive disease resulting from pathogenic CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) pathogenic gene variants. While CF's frequency varies among ethnicities, its epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and mutational profiles in Africa still must be explored due to the absence of a comprehensive public health strategy there. This study postulates that complete sequencing of CFTR using Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT)-based long-read sequencing enhances the diagnostic yield. METHODS AND RESULTS: To amplify ∼25-kb fragments covering the whole CFTR gene (NM_000492.4), we designed 11 primer pairs, and barcoded libraries were prepared and sequenced on ONT flow cells (R10.4.1) using an Mk1C device. Variant pathogenicity was assessed by expressing the variant channel in HEK293 cells and examining expression through immuno-blotting. data.text: PMID 41814120: "CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in the parental iPSC line PCIi033-A to introduce the homozygous mutation p.F508del (c.1521_1523del) in the CFTR gene." (Stem Cell Res, 2026). Abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in the parental iPSC line PCIi033-A to introduce the homozygous mutation p.F508del (c.1521_1523del) in the CFTR gene.. Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive disease caused by mutations in the CFTR gene. Patients carrying the most common mutation, p.F508del, benefit from the triple therapy Kaftrio®. We genome-edited the commercially available iPSC line PCIi033-A (wild-type CFTR) to generate the subclone PCIi033-A-5, which is homozygous for the mutation c.1521_1523del (p.F508del), using CRISPR-SpCas9 tools. PCIi033-A-5 has a normal karyotype and stem cell morphology, is pluripotent, and differentiates into the three germ layers. Introducing this mutation in a parental isogenic iPSC line is essential to demonstrate the feasibility of modeling CF disease after differentiation of the iPS cells into bronchial epithelium.

claims.text: Clinical Interpretation for CFTR c.1521_1523del
The variant CFTR c.1521_1523del (p.F508del) is a well-established pathogenic variant associated with cystic fibrosis (CF).
This variant leads to the deletion of three amino acids (Phe, Leu, and Pro) at positions 507, 508, and 509, resulting in a frameshift and premature termination codon.
The variant is classified as Pathogenic in ClinVar (entry: NM_000492.3(CFTR):c.[1521_1523delCTT;3080T>C]).

The c.1521_1523del variant is strongly associated with CF, a genetic disorder characterized by the production of thick, sticky mucus that can obstruct the lungs and lead to severe respiratory and digestive issues.
The variant disrupts the proper folding and function of the CFTR protein, leading to chloride ion channel dysfunction.
The penetrance of the c.1521_1523del variant is high, with approximately 90-95% of individuals with this variant developing CF.
However, the expressivity can vary, with some individuals showing mild symptoms or even being asymptomatic.

The recent study in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes (CFTR function in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes) suggests that CFTR function may differ between asymptomatic and symptomatic heterozygotes, indicating potential variability in clinical presentation.
Individuals with the c.1521_1523del variant should be managed according to the standard care guidelines for CF.
This includes regular monitoring of lung function, respiratory therapy, nutritional support, and management of complications such as infections.
Genetic counseling is also recommended to inform family members about the risk of inheriting the variant.
The evidence supporting the pathogenicity of the c.1521_1523del variant is strong, with multiple studies and expert panels classifying it as Pathogenic.

The recent study in nasal airway cells provides additional insight into the variability of CFTR function in heterozygotes, but the overall evidence remains consistent with the established pathogenicity of this variant.
The CFTR c.1521_1523del variant is classified as Pathogenic and is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis.
While the penetrance is high, the expressivity can vary, and asymptomatic carriers may exist.
Standard CF management protocols should be followed, and genetic counseling is recommended.
The evidence supporting this classification is robust, based on multiple ClinVar entries and recent research.

data.title: Clinical Interpretation
data.content:
### Clinical Interpretation for CFTR c.1521_1523del

#### 1. Clinical Significance
The variant CFTR c.1521_1523del (p.F508del) is a well-established pathogenic variant associated with cystic fibrosis (CF). This variant leads to the deletion of three amino acids (Phe, Leu, and Pro) at positions 507, 508, and 509, resulting in a frameshift and premature termination codon. The variant is classified as Pathogenic in ClinVar (entry: NM_000492.3(CFTR):c.[1521_1523delCTT;3080T>C]).

#### 2. Disease Associations
The c.1521_1523del variant is strongly associated with CF, a genetic disorder characterized by the production of thick, sticky mucus that can obstruct the lungs and lead to severe respiratory and digestive issues. The variant disrupts the proper folding and function of the CFTR protein, leading to chloride ion channel dysfunction.

#### 3. Penetrance & Expressivity
The penetrance of the c.1521_1523del variant is high, with approximately 90-95% of individuals with this variant developing CF. However, the expressivity can vary, with some individuals showing mild symptoms or even being asymptomatic. The recent study in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes (CFTR function in nasal airway cells from symptomatic and asymptomatic CF heterozygotes) suggests that CFTR function may differ between asymptomatic and symptomatic heterozygotes, indicating potential variability in clinical presentation.

#### 4. Clinical Management
Individuals with the c.1521_1523del variant should be managed according to the standard care guidelines for CF. This includes regular monitoring of lung function, respiratory therapy, nutritional support, and management of complications such as infections. Genetic counseling is also recommended to inform family members about the risk of inheriting the variant.

#### 5. Evidence Quality
The evidence supporting the pathogenicity of the c.1521_1523del variant is strong, with multiple studies and expert panels classifying it as Pathogenic. The recent study in nasal airway cells provides additional insight into the variability of CFTR function in heterozygotes, but the overall evidence remains consistent with the established pathogenicity of this variant.

### Conclusion
The CFTR c.1521_1523del variant is classified as Pathogenic and is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis. While the penetrance is high, the expressivity can vary, and asymptomatic carriers may exist. Standard CF management protocols should be followed, and genetic counseling is recommended. The evidence supporting this classification is robust, based on multiple ClinVar entries and recent research.
